A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EM-for-Mixtures-of-Experts study and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The original two-expert results can be matched across renaming, renumbering, and relocation in v2.

before.justification: Section 6 reports original synthetic regression and Fashion-MNIST experiments, including convergence curves, parameter-recovery results, and classification scores.

after.justification: Section 6 retains original empirical evaluations, and Appendix C.1 adds experiments on grayscale CIFAR-10.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 and Appendix D.4 introduce an EM-like formulation for deep and sparse MoE, using latent expert-selection sequences across layers and a greedy-path approximation to avoid combinatorial evaluation. This substantially extends the proposed procedure, although it is not experimentally validated. Classical EM and Gradient EM remain unchanged; the projected-MD correspondence is an analytical characterization.

E1.justification: Appendix C.1 adds grayscale CIFAR-10 object classification to the retained synthetic regression and original/inverted Fashion-MNIST evaluations. This is a limited domain extension within image classification; the proposed deep/sparse architectures are not separately evaluated.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain EM, Gradient EM, and Gradient Descent, while Table 1 retains the single-logistic-expert controls. CIFAR-10 uses the same optimizer comparison set. Newly discussed methods such as EIM are not evaluated.

E3.justification: The new CIFAR-10 evaluation introduces mini-batch training for 50 epochs with five experts and nonlinear MLP gates/experts, substantially extending the earlier experimental configurations. Retained experiments are newly described as full-batch, which establishes disclosure rather than a setting change. Synthetic Figures 1–2 now extend to 100 iterations instead of 50, but the prose still specifies 50, leaving the actual revised budget unclear.

E4.justification: The Fashion-MNIST inversion controls and existing convergence/parameter-recovery analyses are retained. CIFAR-10 supplies another benchmark comparison, not a controlled ablation, sensitivity study, or robustness test.

E5.justification: v1 reports averages without error bars or significance tests. v2 adds error bars to Figures 1–3 and paired t-tests, reporting T-statistics at least 22 for synthetic results and at least 17 for Fashion-MNIST; CIFAR-10 also includes bars and a paired test. The retained 50/25-instance counts do not establish additional runs. The meaning of the error bars remains unspecified.

E6.justification: Table 2 accuracy/cross-entropy pairs change from 79.2%/0.801 to 78.5%/0.827 for EM, 65.7%/1.30 to 66.0%/1.29 for Gradient EM, and 61.9%/1.33 to 62.4%/1.30 for GD. Synthetic curves are revised and extended. Appendix C.1 adds CIFAR-10 accuracies of 41.6%, 37.4%, and 34.5%, respectively. These substantially expand reported results while retaining the optimizer ranking; Table 1 is unchanged.

T1.justification: New Theorems 4.1–4.2 and Appendix A establish a conditional-exponential-family formulation, expected-KL projection characterization, and convergence bounds with regularity, average-convexity, and projection-inequality assumptions. The original symmetric-two-expert theory largely survives in Section 5 and Appendix B. The simplified parallel-vector SNR derivation in v1 Section 5.2 is removed.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions broaden the central theoretical claim from linear/logistic two-expert models to general MoE with conditionally exponential-family distributions, characterized by projected mirror descent. The original direct-MD and SNR results become special cases. The empirical claim that EM can outperform GD remains.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands applicability qualifications: Appendix A.2 explains that the projection set need not be convex and the required Pythagorean inequality is not automatic; Section 4.2 identifies stochastic/mini-batch guarantees as open; Appendix D.4 discusses combinatorial costs of deep/sparse EM. The earlier simplified best-case SNR interpretation is removed, while most original MIM discussion is retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies retained experiments as full-batch and documents the CIFAR-10 architecture, including 100-unit ReLU hidden layers and unit-row-norm initialization. Appendix D adds explicit standard-EM pseudocode alongside the retained Gradient EM/GD algorithms. These are useful documentation additions, but numerical learning rates, batch size, and inner-loop budgets remain unspecified.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion adds foundational Jacobs et al. work and EIM, clarifies earlier EM-for-MoE results and Makkuva et al.'s frozen-expert procedure, and adds sparse-MoE and mini-batch literature. Positioning relative to Kunstner et al. becomes more explicit. KKS22-to-KKS21 and several other reference changes identify the same works rather than new citations.

P1.justification: The narrative is reorganized around general MoE followed by symmetric special cases. Much of v1's main convergence analysis moves into Appendix B, while the abstract, contributions, and discussion are rewritten. v2 also adds a contents section, notation guide, separate algorithms appendix, and revised symmetric-model terminology.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 are redrawn with error bars and revised displays; synthetic plots extend their horizontal range, and Figure 1b changes from logarithmic to linear vertical scaling. v2 adds CIFAR-10 Figure 4 and an EM algorithm box, reformats existing pseudocode with line numbers, and relocates figures and tables.

improvement.justification: The new general-MoE analysis and explicit projection assumptions address v1's central restriction to symmetric two-expert guarantees, making the broader applicability substantially more assessable. CIFAR-10 adds evidence beyond the engineered two-expert examples, and uncertainty reporting strengthens empirical scrutiny. These gains outweigh remaining reporting weaknesses, including undefined error bars and the synthetic 50-versus-100-iteration inconsistency; the deep/sparse extension remains unvalidated.
